entries.title: II Chronicles 4:1
segments: ¶Moreover he made a bronze altar: twenty cubits was its length, twenty cubits its width, and ten cubits its height.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:2
segments: Then he made the Sea of cast [bronze], ten cubits from one brim to the other; [it was] completely round. Its height [was] five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:3
segments: And under it [was] the likeness of oxen encircling it all around, ten to a cubit, all the way around the Sea. The oxen [were] cast in two rows, when it was cast.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:4
segments: It stood on twelve oxen: three looking toward the north, three looking toward the west, three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; the Sea [was set] upon them, and all their back parts [pointed] inward.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:5
segments: It [was] a handbreadth thick; and its brim was shaped like the brim of a cup, [like] a lily blossom. It contained three thousand baths.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:6
segments: He also made ten lavers, and put five on the right side and five on the left, to wash in them; such things as they offered for the burnt offering they would wash in them, but the Sea [was] for the priests to wash in.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:7
segments: And he made ten lampstands of gold according to their design, and set [them] in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:8
segments: He also made ten tables, and placed [them] in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left. And he made one hundred bowls of gold.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:9
segments: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great court and doors for the court; and he overlaid these doors with bronze.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:10
segments: He set the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:11
segments: ¶Then Huram made the pots and the shovels and the bowls. So Huram finished doing the work that he was to do for King Solomon for the house of God:

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:12
segments: the two pillars and the bowl-shaped capitals [that were] on top of the two pillars; the two networks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals which [were] on top of the pillars;

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:13
segments: four hundred pomegranates for the two networks (two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals that [were] on the pillars);

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:14
segments: he also made carts and the lavers on the carts;

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:15
segments: one Sea and twelve oxen under it;

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:16
segments: also the pots, the shovels, the forks-and all their articles Huram his master [craftsman] made of burnished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:17
segments: In the plain of Jordan the king had them cast in clay molds, between Succoth and Zeredah.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:18
segments: And Solomon had all these articles made in such great abundance that the weight of the bronze was not determined.

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:19
segments: Thus Solomon had all the furnishings made for the house of God: the altar of gold and the tables on which [was] the showbread;

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:20
segments: the lampstands with their lamps of pure gold, to burn in the prescribed manner in front of the inner sanctuary,

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:21
segments: with the flowers and the lamps and the wick-trimmers of gold, of purest gold;

entries.title: II Chronicles 4:22
segments: the trimmers, the bowls, the ladles, and the censers of pure gold. As for the entry of the sanctuary, its inner doors to the Most Holy [Place], and the doors of the main hall of the temple, [were] gold.
